question: Explain the photoelectric effect. Why does emission of photoelectrons not occur below a certain frequency of incident radiation?

options.A: The photoelectric effect is emission of electrons from a metal surface when radiation of suitable frequency falls on it. Below threshold frequency $\nu_0$, each photon has energy $h\nu<\phi_0$, so it cannot overcome the work function and no emission occurs.
options.B: Photoelectric effect is heating of a metal by light. Emission does not occur below threshold frequency because photon momentum is zero.
options.C: Photoelectric effect is the absorption of light by a metal. Emission occurs at all frequencies if intensity is sufficiently large.
options.D: Photoelectric effect is reflection of photons from a metal. Below threshold frequency electrons have no charge.
